text.headline: Bitcoin retreats amid regulatory pressure
text.tone: Digital assets fell sharply as confirmed reports of regulatory actions and exchange-traded fund outflows weighed on market sentiment.
lead: Bitcoin fell 6.6% on Friday, marking a sharp decline on the [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]] page. This move coincided with a 4.6% retreat in US large caps and a 15.8% rise in the VIX volatility index in the latest data. The pattern is consistent with digital assets behaving as risk assets rather than safe havens during periods of equity market stress.

The decline followed confirmed reports of SEC lawsuits and Bitcoin ETF outflows totaling nearly $3.5 billion in November. While these factors weighed on demand, broader market pressure was also evident. The yen firmed as shares fell, a move typical of investors cutting risk, while the USD/CNY rose 0.2% amid trade and tariff concerns.

Metals also saw sharp selling on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]]. Silver slumped 7.4% and gold fell 4.6%, despite hotter inflation data which often supports precious metals. The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] places these moves in the context of a quarter where world stocks have traded below their 200-day average, signaling a broader risk-off regime.

briefs.markets: US large caps fell 4.6% as the VIX volatility index rose to 28.44. Treasury yields showed quiet moves in the latest data, with the 10-year yield at 5.04% on the [[markets|Financial Markets]] page.
briefs.energy: Energy prices remained relatively stable in the latest data from November 17. Brent crude edged up 0.04% to $92.94, while natural gas fell 3.1% on the [[energy|Energy Terminal]].
briefs.crypto: Bitcoin and Ether both lost over 6% following news of SEC lawsuits and significant ETF outflows. The USD/CNY rose 0.2% to 6.6777 on the [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]] page.
briefs.metals: Silver led a broad decline in metals, falling 7.4% to $41.07. Copper dropped 2.7% to $12,230/t, reflecting potential worries about industrial demand on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]].
briefs.estate: The [[estate|Estate Index]] shows divergent global trends, with house prices rising 33.7% in Moldova while falling 6.3% in China and 3.6% in Saudi Arabia.
briefs.corporate: The [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]] identifies APA Corporation as a top-scoring company. This comes as credit spreads remain calm despite the recent volatility in equity markets.
briefs.outlook: The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] for Q4 2026 remains cautious. Semiconductor and AI themes have faced significant pressure, falling 24.8% and 19.4% respectively since the quarter began.
briefs.islamic: The EB Shariah US 100 fell 4.8% on Friday, slightly underperforming the broader market. Shariah-compliant assets represent 59% of the index on the [[islamic|Islamic Investment]] page.

watch: US budget and debt news, as news coverage has increased regarding a potential government shutdown without a corresponding reaction in the Treasury market yet.
The USD/JPY exchange rate, where further yen strength would provide additional evidence of a broader move by investors to reduce risk across asset classes.
Bitcoin ETF flow data for the coming week to determine if the $3.5 billion in November outflows represents a sustained exit from digital asset markets.
